products.name: InternLM (Shanghai AI Lab)
products.note: Chinese open-source LLM; academic research; cross-border data review advised

profile_text.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory (上海人工智能实验室) is a non-profit, government-affiliated research institution based in Shanghai focused on artificial intelligence research and development. The laboratory describes its work as spanning large language models, embodied intelligence, trustworthy and safe AI, AI for Science, and foundational platforms. Since 2022 it has run a joint doctoral training program with more than ten leading Chinese universities, including Peking University, Tsinghua University, Fudan University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tongji University, the University of Science and Technology of China, and Zhejiang University.

The laboratory develops the InternLM family of open-source large language models, which it positions for academic research, and maintains what it calls the "Intern" ecosystem of tools, including the Intern-Robotics full-stack embodied intelligence engine and, announced at the 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference, the Shusheng Duanyan scientific discovery platform. That platform connects scientific large models, specialized agents, experimental data, and embodied automation equipment to cover a research workflow from hypothesis generation through experimental validation. At the same conference the laboratory also released ten joint AI-for-science innovation results with partner universities and research institutions covering life science, materials science, and deep-space astronomy.

On AI safety, the laboratory articulates what it calls the "AI-45° balance law," a framework holding that safety and capability should develop in rough parity over the long term, and it describes pursuing a causality-centered path toward trustworthy AGI through three progressive stages it labels broad alignment, interventionability, and reflectiveness. No litigation or regulatory filings appear in the held facts for this organization.
